pages.title: Open Assets Docs: App Store screenshots and icons from HTML
pages.description: Open Assets turns HTML, CSS and SVG templates into App Store screenshots, app icons, OG images and favicons, rendered at every size from one local CLI.

pages.title: Claude Code | Open Assets Docs
pages.description: Install the Open Assets skill in Claude Code from the plugin marketplace, with npx open-assets skills, or the Skills CLI, and learn what the agent does with it.

pages.title: GitHub Actions | Open Assets Docs
pages.description: Render App Store screenshots and icons in GitHub Actions with Open Assets: validate, render incrementally with assets.lock, then commit or upload the PNGs.

pages.title: Collections | Open Assets Docs
pages.description: A collection groups templates that share one source size and one list of export sizes. Learn its fields, how filtering works and how it maps to dev tabs.

pages.title: Examples | Open Assets Docs
pages.description: Six real Open Assets projects from shipped apps, with App Store screenshots, icons, Product Hunt galleries and social headers you can clone, run and copy from.

pages.title: Cat IQ Test | Open Assets Docs
pages.description: The Cat IQ Test example: App Store screenshots, a Product Hunt gallery at 1x and 2x, an app icon and an SVG logo exported with copy-source, all in one project.

pages.title: Upload to App Store Connect | Open Assets Docs
pages.description: Map Open Assets export folders to App Store Connect and Google Play screenshot slots, then upload by hand or automate it with fastlane deliver or an asc CLI.

pages.title: Localization | Open Assets Docs
pages.description: Render localized App Store screenshots in every language from one set of HTML templates, with string placeholders, fallbacks, number formatting and RTL text.

pages.title: Fonts for Localized Screenshots | Open Assets Docs
pages.description: Make Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Arabic and Hebrew text render the same on every machine by bundling webfonts and choosing font stacks per language with :lang().

pages.title: Migrate from frameit | Open Assets Docs
pages.description: Move App Store screenshots from fastlane frameit to Open Assets: map frames, Framefile.json titles and strings to templates, collections and localizations.

pages.title: CLI reference | Open Assets Docs
pages.description: Every open-assets command with its arguments, global flags, exit codes and how the optional dir argument picks the project folder that holds assets.json.

pages.title: Changelog | Open Assets Docs
pages.description: User-facing changes in each Open Assets release, from 0.2.0 to 0.5.1: localization, the locale picker, faster parallel renders, the plugin, and fixes.

pages.title: Installation | Open Assets Docs
pages.description: Install the Open Assets CLI as a dev dependency or run it with npx. Covers the Node version requirement, the Chromium download and how to verify the install.

pages.title: Shell alias and editor setup | Open Assets Docs
pages.description: Shorten the Open Assets command with a shell alias, add npm scripts for dev and render with Tailwind, and set up your editor and gitignore for a smooth loop.

pages.title: Project structure | Open Assets Docs
pages.description: How an Open Assets project is laid out on disk, from assets.json and template folders to public, dist, exports, assets.lock and localizations.json files.

pages.title: Tutorial: your first screenshot set | Open Assets Docs
pages.description: Build a three-screenshot App Store set with a shared stylesheet, render it at iPhone 6.9 and 6.7 inch sizes, and write an app icon into an Xcode asset catalog.
